statement.p: Find the Jacobian. \frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}, where x = 3s-t+4u, y = 3u-\left(3s+t\right), z = 2s-3t-4u.

static.solution: \left|\frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}\right| = \left|\begin{array}{ccc} x_s \amp x_t \amp x_u\\ y_s \amp y_t \amp y_u\\ z_s \amp z_t \amp z_u \end{array}\right| =\left|\begin{array}{ccc} 3 \amp -1 \amp 4\\ -3 \amp -1 \amp 3\\ 2 \amp -3 \amp -4 \end{array}\right|. This 3 \times 3 determinant is computed the same way as for the cross product, with the entries 3,-1,4 in the first row playing the same role as \vec i,\vec j,\vec k. We get \frac{\partial (x,y,z)}{\partial (s,t,u)}= ((-1)(-4)-(3)(-3))3 + ((3)(2)-(-3)(-4))-1 + ((-3)(-3)-(-1)(2))4 = 89.
